description: P09.06: what data this platform holds, why, how long, who may see it, and what residual privacy risk remains. Each category is checked against the live database and the contracts by verify_data_inventory.py, not asserted from memory - retention_class values must match database/retention.py's own windows, privacy_classification values must be in the device/observation-envelope contract enum, and every distinct (device_type, privacy_classification, retention_class) combination actually present in a live database must be covered by some category.

categories.title: Roadway and vulnerable-road-user sensor telemetry
categories.purpose: Real-time traffic state (counts, speeds, occupancy, queue length) for the live map, analytics, forecasting and incident detection.
categories.minimization: A device reports a count, a speed, a binary detection or an occupancy state for its own fixed location - never a vehicle or person identifier. `bluetooth_wifi_sensor` and `connected_vehicle_gateway` are the two types in this list capable of observing a device-level identifier upstream; this platform's contract for them (`contracts/observation-envelope/v1`) carries no such field, so one is never accepted even if a real sensor sent it (P05.05 ingestion validates against the schema and rejects unknown fields).
categories.data_subject: The travelling public, not identified or identifiable from what is collected.
categories.rights_process: Not personal data as collected; no access/erasure process applies. If a future sensor type could report an identifier, it would first need its own contract field, its own privacy_classification, and its own entry here - not silently ride in under this category.

categories.title: Signal, sign and environmental device state
categories.purpose: Operate and monitor field infrastructure the platform can act on (signal phase, VMS message) or that informs decisions (weather).
categories.minimization: Device and environmental state only - phase, message text the operator wrote, temperature/visibility readings. Nothing about a person.

categories.title: Edge camera / LiDAR aggregate track metadata
categories.purpose: Vulnerable-road-user counts and speeds for the same analytics traffic sensors feed, from a device type capable of raw imagery.
categories.minimization: The privacy-preserving pipeline (`source-code/edge/vision_privacy.py`, P04.06) is the ONLY path an edge_camera's data may reach this platform through: privacy zones drop a track point before aggregation with no code path around them, a rehashed non-persistent id (fresh salt every window) is never exported, and a k-anonymity floor suppresses any window with too few contributing objects to reveal one individual. No raw frame, trajectory, face or plate field exists anywhere in this codebase.
categories.data_subject: Pedestrians and cyclists in view of a camera, made anonymous by construction before the platform ever sees a record.
categories.rights_process: Not personal data as received (aggregated, k-anonymous, no persistent id). A rights request about a specific individual could not be answered from platform data even in principle, because no individual-level record is ever created.
categories.residual_risk_note: Correctness of privacy-zone configuration and the k-anonymity floor is what stands between a real camera and identifiable output; both are enforced in code and covered by tests (`tests/test_edge_vision_privacy.py`), but this is a structural guarantee about THIS pipeline, not a guarantee about a camera's raw feed before it reaches this code - deploying a real camera needs its own device-level review. No edge_camera is part of the current simulated device population (0 registered in either database or the sensor catalog); the pipeline is built and tested ahead of that device type actually appearing.

categories.title: Operator, dispatcher and service account identity
categories.purpose: Attribute every safety-relevant action (request, approve, execute, override, audit read) to a real, accountable identity - the basis the whole command-safety path and the audit trail depend on.
categories.minimization: A username and an operating role - nothing else is collected by this platform (no additional profile field, no contact detail, no location of the person). Demo identities' passwords are generated at provisioning time into a git-ignored file, never committed, never logged.
categories.data_subject: Platform operators, dispatchers, supervisors, auditors and demo presenters - staff, not the public.
categories.rights_process: Handled through the operating organisation's ordinary HR/IT identity process (Keycloak account management), out of scope for this platform; CTL-46 (joiner-mover-leaver review, P09.07) is the platform-side control over who holds an account at all.
categories.residual_risk_note: Retention class 'audit' means this is never purged by `database/retention.py` - a deliberate, accepted design decision (safety-critical action accountability), not an oversight: see the retention_class ACCEPTED note below.

categories.title: Emergency call and unit assignment records
categories.purpose: Coordinate dispatch: call type/priority/location, unit assignment, route and status, for real-time response and later review.
categories.minimization: `contracts/emergency-call/v1` and `contracts/emergency-unit-assignment/v1` carry no caller name, phone number or crew-member identifier field - checked directly against the schema by this task's verifier, not merely stated. A location is present (where the call concerns, not where a person live-tracks); `unit_id` identifies a vehicle/resource, not a person.
categories.data_subject: A caller and the people at an incident location, indirectly and only through the location and call type, never by name or contact detail.
categories.rights_process: No identifier is collected to look one up by; a rights request about a specific incident would be answered through the operating agency's own CAD/records process, not this platform, which never receives that identifier in the first place.

categories.title: Policy decisions, command history and override justifications
categories.purpose: Independent, tamper-evident proof of what was decided, by whom, under which policy version, and why - the safety and accountability record P09.03/P09.05 build.
categories.minimization: Structured fields (target, action type, safety class, decision) plus one piece of free text a person writes by hand: an override's mandatory justification. That text is redacted for secrets before storage (CTL-16) but is not otherwise shortened or paraphrased - minimizing it further would remove the reason the control exists to capture.
categories.data_subject: The operator who wrote the justification.
categories.rights_process: Same as operator-and-service-identity: append-only and never purged by design; not subject to an erasure request, for the same reason a flight recorder is not.

categories.title: Demo identities and scenario-control runs
categories.purpose: Presentation and testing, structurally separate from every operational category above (P05.09, P08.09).
categories.minimization: Nine synthetic usernames with a generated password each, regenerated by `provision.py` and never committed; the `demo_operator` identity holds no operational capability at all.
categories.data_subject: Whoever is running the demo (typically the platform's own operators, not the public).
categories.rights_process: Not applicable - synthetic accounts, regenerated at will.

used_by: not currently assigned to any category above
short.note: reserved for the highest-volume, shortest-lived data the schema allows; nothing in the current device population needs a window this short.

standard.note: the default operational window: long enough for trend analytics and incident review, short enough to bound what is kept.

used_by: not currently assigned to any category above
extended.note: reserved for a data class needing a year for seasonal comparison; none of the current live data uses it.

audit.note: never purged (`database/retention.py` refuses to touch it) and, since P09.05, hash-chained and append-only - an ACCEPTED design decision: safety-critical accountability outweighs minimization for this narrow set of pseudonymous (username-level) records, and nothing in this class is public-facing personal data.

dpia_summary.reasoning: No special-category data is collected (no health, biometric-identity, political or similar data). The one identifiable-in-principle path (edge camera imagery) is structurally prevented from producing individual-level output before it ever reaches the platform (P04.06). The only personal data actually held is staff identity at username granularity, kept for safety accountability.
dpia_summary.not_claimed: This is a research/demonstration platform. No production personal-data processing, no real jurisdiction's legal basis, and no certification to any privacy framework is claimed anywhere in this document or elsewhere in the project.
